newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen soar to uncharted highs.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen soar to uncharted highs.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) futures and Euroyen futures traded to their record highs for the third consecutive day on Monday since the Bank of Japan's (BOJ's) tankan last Wednesday, dealers said.
"JGBs are on a strong uptrend with very strong buying interest seen. You don't want to be caught short now," one dealer with a European institution said.
Dealers said a continued flow of funds into JGBs helped boost the market into uncharted levels.
After opening at 126.37, December JGBs soared to new highs at 126.90, before settling at 126.93. Turnover was 1,131 lots.
Dealers said JGBs witnessed some sell-off after BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita's comments that two of BOJ's three monetary policy aims had "just about been achieved".
However, dealers short-covered after they realised the governor was still not ready to concede that Japan's economy was back on a self-sustainable recovery track.
"Earlier it was not clear which one of the three aims had not been achieved and that spooked the market," the dealer said.
Dealers pegged psychological support for December JGBs at 127.00.
They awaited Japan's Economic Planning Agency's announcement of the third quarter gross domestic product figures at 0630 GMT on Tuesday for clearer direction.

General market consensus was for the July-September GDP to fall by an average of 0.05 percent in real terms from the previous quarter. Japan's GDP showed a quarter-on-quarter fall of 0.7 percent in April-June period.
"If we get a number that is below the consensus or at flat to negative, JGBs are going to go through the roof and the Nikkei will fall to test 20,100," the dealer said.
After opening at its previous IMM close, June Euroyen surged its day high at 99.37, four ticks off its IMM close. Turnover was around 9,980 lots.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.46 againsts its IMM close at 94.47 on a turnover of 3,945 lots.
